newsitem.title: USA: Fibreboard sees Q4 net below expectations.
newsitem.headline: Fibreboard sees Q4 net below expectations.

text.p: Fibreboard Corp said it expects to see a reduction in earnings in the fourth quarter of this year and the first quarter of 1997, compared to prior expectations.
It did not provide details. The company also said it completed the sale of its resort group to Booth Creek Inc for about $126 million, including the assumption of certain liabilities by Booth Creek.

The transaction, which included Northstar-at-Tahoe, Sierra-at-Tahoe and Bear Mountain ski resorts, generated approximately $92 million in after-tax cash proceeds, which Fibreboard plans to use to fund the next phase of its aggressive internal growth and strategic acquisition program.
The company said it believes it will "achieve greater growth and value over time as a result of this transaction."
It said it was "optimistic the acquisition program will replace lost Resort Group earnings..."
"In the short term, we will miss the earnings generated by the resort group over the next four months," it said in a statement.
"We now have over $200 million immediately available to fund our acquisition program," it said.
It said its strategy includes acquiring building products companies that need capital and expanded distribution access in order to secure a leadership market position.

Fibreboard said after-tax cash proceeds from the sale of the resort group is approximately $92 million, with a gain of about $35 million, or approximately $4 per share. Resultant book value per share is approximately $33.
Effective in the fourth quarter, the resort group will be recorded as a discontinued operation, and financial statements for prior periods will be restated, it said.

The earnings contribution from the resort group was estimated at $0.20-$0.25 per share for the fourth quarter, and $0.55-$0.65 for the first quarter of 1997. The overall impact is $0.40-$0.45 for full year 1997 earnings.
Fibreboard said it's now solely focused on market leadership and aggressive growth in the building products industry.
